name: Quantum information: shallow-circuit Ising ground states
description: Optimize parameters of a fixed three-layer Ry/CZ circuit to approximate ground states of open transverse-field Ising chains. The evaluator builds each state itself and minimizes the mean energy gap per spin relative to an independent exact eigensolution.

sources.locator: Peruzzo et al. (2014), variational eigenvalue estimation and Rayleigh-Ritz energy minimization.
Kandala et al. (2017), hardware-efficient variational circuits and quantum magnetism application; motivation rather than a copied ansatz.

requirements.datasets: None downloaded; mathematical constructions or locally generated synthetic instances.

evaluation.benchmark: Quantum information: shallow-circuit Ising ground states
evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: angles(n, coupling, field, layers) -> finite real array (layers,n) in radians. H=-coupling*sum Z_i Z_(i+1)-field*sum X_i, open chain, qubit i is bit i. Start |0>^n; each layer applies Ry(theta) to every qubit; between layers apply CZ on every adjacent pair in ascending order. No entangler after final layer. Fixed layers=3, n=4,6, coupling=1, fields=0.45,1,1.65. Objective: mean (circuit energy - exact ground energy)/n. Development fields: 0.3,0.8,1.4. Return circuit parameters, not a statevector or reported energy.

limitations: The open Ising Hamiltonian, exact Ry/CZ ansatz, field values and statevector simulator are local reduced choices, not the molecular experiments in the papers.
No noise, measurement cost or hardware connectivity penalty is modeled. A lower circuit energy does not establish a new physical ground-state result or quantum advantage.
The minimum within the restricted ansatz can exceed the exact ground energy; zero error is not assumed reachable.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Optimize a fixed three-layer variational circuit for small open-chain Ising Hamiltonians.
